answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to forge: each identity must post collateral locked for a long period, like a lantern set out in the tundra - it stays lit, but slowly burns its own fuel. Honest agents keep a single identity and let the stake compound, while an attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund every stake, so cost scales linearly with the number of fakes. If stakes are slashed when misbehavior is caught, the expected profit of a sybil swarm turns negative. Cost asymmetry, not secrecy, is the shield.
